text.p: Australian gas and oil producer Santos Ltd announced on Wednesday that it planned to boost its exploration effort to record levels in calendar 1997.

Santos plans to spend A$173 million in 1997 on exploration, over half of it outside its traditional hunting ground of Australia's onshore Cooper basin, managing director Ross Adler told reporters in Melbourne.
"The exploration budget for 1997 is an all-time record," he said. Exploration expenditure in 1996 totalled A$121 million.

The 1997 exploration programme signals a major shift away from the Cooper basin to other onshore Australian basins as well as to fields off northwest Australia and in neighbouring Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, Adler said.
Discoveries of the Stag oil field in the Carnarvon basin offshore Western Australia and the Elang/Kakatua fields in the Timor Sea have changed the complexion of Santos, Adler said.
Santos has an involvement in both projects, which are scheduled to begin production in 1998.
Adler said Santos had now answered criticism of its record of exploration success outside the Cooper basin, citing an overall success rate of 57 percent in 1996.
"Fifty-seven percent of the wells we drill find economically recoverable reserves of hydrocarbons," he said.
Santos suggested it was well positioned to share in further discoveries off northwest Australia, one of the hottest regions in the world for oil and gas exploration.
"We are involved in more permits in that area than any other company...," Adler said.
"Generally speaking we have relatively high equity in our permits, so we are very well placed," he said.
"There's been a series of discoveries (there) and we are certainly putting a major emphasis on it," he added.
